html:
Company: E-bikes producer · Home country: Vietnam · Size: Small (<50 staff) · HS 871160 (Vehicles & transport equipment) · Trade data 2019-2024

1. Executive Summary

Verdict: ENTER WITH CAUTION. Real opportunity, but specific risks need a mitigation plan before scaling.

Market attractiveness: 6.3/10
Recommended entry mode: Indirect / direct exporting via importers and distributors

  • Import market of €1.57 bn in 2024, trend growth +1.6% a year (data confidence: high).
  • Supply is highly concentrated (HHI 3,476); top supplier China holds 53.5%.
  • CAGE distance from Vietnam: high.
  • Applicable import duty: 2.5% (Preferential rate under EU-Vietnam FTA, published by WITS for 2021 (rules of origin apply; MFN 6.0% otherwise)); landed cost ≈ +14% over ex-works price before VAT.
  • Vietnam is supplier #3 with 8.08% of imports, priced premium (1.7x market average per kg).
  • China supplies 53.5% of extra-EU imports.
  • Priority EU markets: Austria, Germany, Netherlands.

2. Market Size & Growth

Market size is measured as imports into EU-27 (Eurostat Comext DS-045409 (extra-EU imports)). Imports show demand served from abroad, not total consumption.

Growth 2019-2024: trend +1.59% a year (log-linear fit over all years); end-point CAGR +0.23%.

Data confidence: High. No quality issues detected.

Seasonality

Monthly extra-EU imports relative to the yearly average (100), 2022–2024:

Strong seasonality (peak-to-trough 58 points). Peak months: May, Jun, Jul; quietest: Nov, Jan, Dec. With 6-8 weeks of sea freight, ship in Mar and Apr to have stock in place for the peak.

  • Trade agreement: EU-Vietnam FTA gives preferential access if rules of origin are met.

4. PESTEL Analysis

  • Political: Stable democracies with a single trade policy run by the European Commission. EU-China relations follow a 'de-risking' agenda: more trade-defence cases, the Foreign Subsidies Regulation and screening of Chinese investment. Vehicles are a flashpoint in EU-China trade policy.
  • Economic: Single market of ~450 million consumers and one of the world's largest import markets; high purchasing power, though growth is modest and varies strongly between member states. Latest: GDP growth 1.5% (2025), inflation 2.5% (World Bank).
  • Social: Diverse languages and consumer cultures across 27 countries; strong demand for sustainability, quality and data privacy; ageing population.
  • Technological: Advanced digital infrastructure and e-commerce; strict standards (CE, EN norms) make quality and certification a competitive factor.
  • Environmental: European Green Deal: CBAM, Ecodesign/ESPR, Battery Regulation, deforestation and packaging rules raise compliance costs but reward low-carbon products. Electrification targets support EV and e-mobility demand.
  • Legal: Harmonised product law across the EU (one CE mark for 27 markets), GDPR for customer data, strong IP protection and contract enforcement.

5. CAGE Distance

Dimension Distance Evidence
Cultural Medium The EU spans 24 official languages; expect local-language marketing, labels and service in each priority country.
Administrative Medium Preferential access via EU-Vietnam FTA; rules of origin apply.
Geographic High ~8,979 km between capitals. Long lead times (Asia-Europe sea freight ~30-45 days; China-Europe rail ~15-20 days).
Economic High GDP per capita $5,066 (home) vs $47,089 (target), ratio 9.3x.

Overall distance: High.

6. Tariffs, Trade Defence & Regulation

Import duty

  • MFN applied tariff of EU-27: 6%, 2023 (World Bank WITS / UNCTAD TRAINS (MFN applied, simple average)).
  • Likely rate for a company from Vietnam: 2.5% (Preferential rate under EU-Vietnam FTA, published by WITS for 2021 (rules of origin apply; MFN 6.0% otherwise)).

⚠️ Trade policy note (checked 2026-11-21): EU anti-dumping and anti-subsidy duties on e-bikes from China have applied since 2019 (check the current rate and any expiry review). Official source.

Indicative landed cost (per 100 of ex-works value)

Item Amount Assumption
Goods (ex-works) 100.00
Freight & insurance 10.00 10% for high distance
Import duty 2.75 2.5% on CIF value
Clearance, broker, port 1.50 1.5%
Import VAT 22.55 20% (Austria), usually recoverable for VAT-registered importers
Landed cost 136.80 114.25 before VAT (+14.2%)

Regulatory checklist

  • EU type-approval (Reg. 2018/858 for cars; Reg. 168/2013 for L-category vehicles such as speed e-bikes)
  • EN 15194 standard and CE marking (Machinery) for pedal-assist e-bikes
  • EU Battery Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 for traction and light-means-of-transport batteries
  • General Product Safety Regulation (EU) 2023/988 (GPSR), applies to consumer products since Dec 2024
  • Union Customs Code: an EU-established importer/representative and EORI number are required
  • Forced Labour Regulation (EU) 2024/3015: ban on products made with forced labour, applies from Dec 2027

Official texts: Vehicle type-approval, Reg. (EU) 2018/858 · Battery Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 · GPSR, Regulation (EU) 2023/988 · Union Customs Code · Forced Labour Regulation (EU) 2024/3015

Regulatory notes compiled 2026-11-21 from official sources; not legal advice.

Verify current duties and requirements: - Access2Markets (EU tariffs, rules of origin, requirements) - EU TARIC tariff database - EU trade defence cases

7. Risk Matrix

Exchange rate (ECB reference rates): The ECB does not publish VND reference rates.

Risk Likelihood Impact Mitigation
Dominant incumbent supplier (China, 53.5% share) High High Differentiate on quality, service, sustainability and EU/China-specific certification rather than price.
Trade-defence or retaliation measures in the EU-China corridor High High Monitor trade-defence notices; diversify sourcing and production locations; build tariff scenarios into pricing.
Logistics disruption (Red Sea, port congestion, freight-rate swings) Medium Medium Use mixed sea/rail routing, safety stock in a regional hub, Incoterms that share freight risk.
Brand and message mis-fit with local consumers Medium Medium Local consumer testing, native-language content, local marketplace and social channels.
Currency volatility (VND/EUR) Medium Medium Price in home currency where possible; hedge large contracts with forwards.

8. Recommended Entry Mode

Indirect / direct exporting via importers and distributors

  • Moderate attractiveness or high distance favour a low-commitment, reversible entry.
  • Keeps capital at risk low while you learn the market.
  • Your home country already supplies 8.08% of this market (rank 3): existing importers and logistics routes lower the cost of entry, so partner with established importers first.
  • Home-country exports are priced above the market average: position on quality and brand, with selective distribution.
  • Within the EU one CE-compliant product and one importer of record give access to all 27 markets: start with 2-3 priority countries.
  • Inputs: attractiveness 6.3/10, CAGE distance high, institutional quality 6.8/10, company size small (<50 staff).

Sensitivity to the weights

The weights are a judgement call, so the same sub-scores are re-weighted under alternative schemes:

Weighting scheme Score
Base case 6.3
Equal weights 6.3
Size-led (large incumbents) 6.3
Growth-led (start-ups) 6.1

Niche entrant (openness first) 6.3

Robust: the score stays between 6.1 and 6.4, and the verdict band does not change.

10. 90-Day Action Plan

  1. Days 1-30, validate: confirm the HS code and duty rate on official tariff tools, size the niche with customer interviews, shortlist 10 potential partners or channels in Austria, Germany, Netherlands.
  2. Days 1-30, compliance: map required certifications and labelling (see section 6), get quotes from a test lab or regulatory agent, register trademarks in the target market.
  3. Days 31-60, commercial model: build a landed-cost and pricing model (duties, freight, VAT, channel margins, FX), and draft the partner or channel agreement.
  4. Days 31-60, go-to-market: localise product pages, packaging and sales material; pick 1-2 launch channels consistent with the entry mode: indirect / direct exporting via importers and distributors.
  5. Days 61-90, pilot: ship a pilot order or open the online store, track sell-through, margin and customer feedback against go/no-go KPIs.
